assumptions: Claude Code with dynamic workflows enabled (v2.1.154 or later; v2.1.309 documented) and not disabled by the organization; native plugin installed with a registered workspace; sources are committed work; unconfirmed host behaviors (HV-1..HV-5) are assumed absent until observed; no paid API spend (EUR 0 beyond the founder's existing Claude subscription).
compatibility: Additive and Claude-only: a workflows/ component in the native plugin; no change to AIM, analysis-report, runtime, grant or MCP contracts, to the five product skills or setup skill, or to the Codex manifest. Requires an ADR 0024 amendment (feature-local adr-proposal.md, not adopted). Until adoption the builder excludes workflows/ by default (explicit engineering-only opt-in). Next plugin version would be 0.1.0-alpha.4; no release or publication in this delivery.
domain: Committed Git work of at most 32 operations in one registered analysis-only workspace, observed at file-level resource granularity through existing read-only analyzers; replay and prepare only for 2 to 4 operations; no transcript, read-effect or uncommitted-work observation.
execution_contract: Planning only in this delivery. The future workflow performs read-only analysis, replay evidence and a non-allocating prepare step through the existing plugin MCP (analyze-work, analyze, prepare; the bundled CLI only on the constrained fallback), spawns at most four sequential agents without worktree isolation under fixed hardened Git commands, refuses runtime-enabled registrations, requires a host permission allowlist, and never issues or uses a grant, executes the owned runtime, edits files, applies merges, creates refs or installs hooks. executionAuthorization is always false.
hypotheses: H1 (hypothesis; no observation exists, may be false): on histories limited to added or modified files the analyzer's conflicting set may contain the merge-tree conflicting set; the expected reason is that the analyzer is file-level, which is a reason to expect it and not a result; H2 (packaging statement, not a detection hypothesis): at commit level the Agent Braid primary flag equals path overlap plus unknown labelling, so no detection advantage over path-only worktree tools or naive overlap is hypothesized; H2 states only that the packaging (labelled file-level evidence, a bounded replay certificate for at most four operations, refusal controls and stated limits) may be useful, and no requirement tests it; neither is a requirement to obtain a positive result, and counterexamples or null results are valid reports.
observation_contract: Pinned base and source commit identifiers, per-phase status, analyzer report and coverage, replay certificate digests or skip reason, prepared batch reference, per-pair merge-tree outcome from fixed hardened Git commands, end-of-run reference re-resolution (stale references), agent count and the assurance block; the host version is listed as unobserved by the script and bound by host receipts; absent observations are reported as unavailable, never as clean.

scenarios.given: the gate runs under any permission mode
scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure for REQ-016/SC-016: exact commands, hashes, failures and limits recorded as obtained evidence only after execution.
scenarios.then: (a) the script refuses with `runtime-enabled-workspace` when any registered workspace has runtime enabled or a grant store, because the plugin MCP then lists model-callable `execute`, `recover`, `verify` and `status` tools next to the gate's own (the tool definitions are the union over registered workspaces) and a script-computed prompt is not a concurrency or authority control (Article 12; ADR 0021: host approval is not runtime authority); (b) on the MCP path the recipe and the host receipts require a host permission allowlist that allows only the plugin tools `workspaces`, `analyze-work`, `analyze` and `prepare` the fixed hardened read-only Git command templates, the exact scratch creation command `mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/braid-gate.XXXXXXXX"` and `rm -rf --` of one `braid-gate.XXXXXXXX` path directly under `TMPDIR` (the only writes, a temporary directory outside the repository; the agent checks the path pattern before removal and reports `removed`, `failed` or `refused`, and a scratch that was not removed is a stated limit that prevents certification); a host that cannot express the last two narrowly makes the baseline phase unavailable (a recorded no-go), not unhardened, with the exact visible tool names recorded in HV-1 and HV-5; (c) the validate agent reports, under a strict schema, the plugin tool names visible to it, and the script refuses with `unsafe-tool-surface` when `execute`, `recover`, `verify` or `status` is among them instead of relying on instructions (an agent-reported defensive check, not enforcement; HV-1 records whether the host can deny them); (d) the constrained Bash is defined once, here and in the Clarifications: a host permission rule set in force for the session that allows only the fixed read-only Git prefixes and explicit launcher subcommands from a closed list, never the launcher binary as a whole, because the launcher also exposes grant and execute subcommands; for gate v1 the closed list is `analyze-git`, `plan-git`, `verify-git` and the read-only registry read `plugin workspaces` with no further arguments, admitted only on the constrained-CLI fallback (MCP tools not visible to workflow agents, HV-1); gate v2 (SPEC-053, blocked by G0) would add exactly one more explicit subcommand, `analyze-claude-transcripts`, usable alongside working MCP tools, as a planning amendment approved by the founder on 2026-10-24; (e) on the constrained-CLI fallback the registry rules are computed from the rows printed by `plugin workspaces` (the same fields as the MCP bootstrap tool, read live instead of from the connect-time snapshot): `workspace-not-registered`, `workspace-root-mismatch` and `runtime-enabled-workspace` apply unchanged, the `unsafe-tool-surface` check applies to any plugin tool names the validate agent reports, and the Bash allowlist, which the script cannot observe, is the only control for the launcher; the fallback refuses with `mcp-unavailable` when the registry rows cannot be obtained or parsed, and is a recorded no-go unless HV-5 recorded that the host can express the allowlist

scientific_limits: No acceptance evidence obtained. File-level analysis is coarser than hunk merging and ignores reads; deletions, renames, binaries and symlinks are unknown effects; uncommitted work is invisible; parallel runtime speedup is a recorded NO-GO and no speed claim is made; fixture agreement does not generalize to real workloads (Article 19) until a real multi-worktree observation exists; structural checks are not proof of semantic safety.
scope: Package a read-only Claude dynamic workflow (/agent-braid:braid-gate) in the native plugin that, given a base and committed sources from worktree agents, returns Agent Braid evidence through the plugin MCP analyze-work, analyze and prepare tools plus a git merge-tree baseline (ephemeral, never applied) and, for 2 to 4 operations, replay evidence and a prepared batch, with executionAuthorization false, an Article 13 assurance block and a tool surface restricted by registration mode and host allowlist.
